name: Efficient Motor Driver Benchmark
desc: Four drivers share one motor, each used as a low-side switch. One after the other they switch it fully on while the divider measures the voltage lost across the switch: the lower the loss, the more of the 6 V reaches the motor. A ranking is printed. (The kit has no tachometer, so delivered voltage replaces measured speed.)
circuit: TIP122: base <- D9 via 1k, emitter -> GND, collector -> motor (low-side switch, 1N4007 flyback diode across the motor)
IRFZ44N: gate <- D10 via 220 ohm, source -> GND, drain -> motor (low-side switch, 1N4007 flyback diode across the motor)
L293D: pin 16 + EN -> logic 5V, pin 8 -> +6V pack, GND pins -> GND; EN1,2 <- D6 (PWM), 1A <- A1, 2A <- A2
L298N channel A: ENA <- D5 (PWM), IN1 <- D4, IN2 <- D7; 12V terminal <- +6V pack, GND <- GND, 5V pin <- Uno 5V (logic)
Motor-node monitor: 10k + 10k divider from the switched (low-side) motor terminal to A0 (A0 reads half of that voltage)
4xAA pack (6 V): + -> bottom red rail (+6V), - -> bottom blue rail (GND), joined to the Uno GND

name: Pan-Tilt Style Sequencer
desc: The stepper is the pan base, the servo the tilt arm. HOLD the button to jog the selected axis (it reverses each time). Taps within 0.6 s: 1 = save a waypoint, 2 = switch axis (base / arm), 3 = replay the recorded sequence, any press stops the replay. Red = recording, green = replaying.
circuit: ULN2003 stepper board: + -> +6V pack, - -> GND, IN1-IN4 <- A1-A4
